title: Escape Pod Ending
textLines: You turn away from the body—your body—and clutch the datapad tighter, forcing yourself to breathe.
You can't stay here. Not another second.
The ship creaks again, a deep, slow sound that feels almost alive. Somewhere far below, metal shears against metal.
The lights flicker and dim to a dull crimson.
You run.
The corridors twist past in a blur of flashing warnings and dead terminals.
The datapad's navigation overlay flickers with every few steps, but the glowing indicator for the Escape Pods stays mercifully solid.
A few turns later, you reach the pod bay.
Inside, the room is nearly empty—rows of empty docking rings, one open pod waiting near the far wall. The others are gone.
You stumble inside.
The pod's systems hum weakly to life as you slam the hatch shut.
Lights crawl across the control panel. A synthetic voice echoes through the small cabin:
AUTOMATED LAUNCH SEQUENCE — MANUAL OVERRIDE ENABLED
LIFE SUPPORT ACTIVE — 2 HOURS REMAINING.
NAVIGATION LOCKED.
You slam your hand onto the LAUNCH button. Explosive bolts fire. The pod shudders violently, then blasts free from the docking clamp.
The artificial gravity cuts out instantly. You float up against the restraints, weightless. Silence rushes in to replace the alarms.
You pull yourself toward the small, thick glass of the viewport to look back at the ship. You expect to see the ship drifting in the quiet dark of space.
But the dark isn't quiet. And it isn’t empty.

Your breath catches in your throat. Behind the shrinking silhouette of your ship, the stars aren't points of light—they are smears. Long, curved streaks of white and blue are being dragged across the sky like wet paint.
And in the center of the distortion, there is a hole in the universe.
It is colossal. A sphere of absolute, impossible blackness, crowned by a halo of burning, shredded matter. It doesn't look like a celestial object; it looks like a mouth.
The ship isn't just drifting. It's falling. And so are you.

The realization hits you harder than the g-force. The groaning metal, the gravity fluctuations, the time dilation—you aren't just stranded. You are caught in the accretion disk of a supermassive singularity
Then the datapad, floating near your head, flickers one last time. A single line of text appears across the cracked display:
PROJECT AEQUALIS — ACTIVE SESSION: 2
You frown. The number blinks.
The pod begins to rattle. A low hum builds—first like an engine, then like a heartbeat.
The stars outside twist and elongate. The viewport's edges ripple as if the glass were melting.
Outside, the black hole expands across your vision, swallowing everything.
The viewport fractures. You feel the ship stretch, reality peeling at the seams.
Your breath freezes midair as the black hole pulls everything forward.
The stars vanish.
Light collapses.
You fall through yourself, through the pod, through the moment—
And then there is nothing.
